report.title: Release-time re-execution of the supply-chain scanners as a time-sensitivity proof
report.question: Does the release gate re-run the vulnerability and license scanners at release time, or does it accept a stored result from implementation time -- and can that difference be demonstrated with a real advisory published in between?
report.headline_answer: IT ACCEPTS A STORED RESULT. The scanners never execute at release time because no release-time event exists (zero release triggers, zero tag triggers, zero releases ever cut, and no schedule on quality.yml); the active ruleset requires the gate-deps (osv-scanner) context but sets strict_required_status_checks_policy=False, so a green computed on a stale head is accepted at merge; and the measured blind window between consecutive gate executions on main reached 205.51 hours (8.56 days). The difference IS demonstrable: injecting a synthetic advisory into a local OSV mirror between two executions of the gate's exact scan-args flipped it green -> red -> green, so the SCANNER is time-sensitive and the STALENESS IS THE WORKFLOW'S, NOT THE SCANNER'S. There is additionally no license scanner in the gate set at all.

extensions.self_hash_convention: artifacts[0].sha256 is the sha256 of THIS FILE'S bytes with the 64 hex characters of that same field replaced by 64 '0' characters. A naive verbatim re-hash will therefore MISMATCH; that is disclosed, not accidental, because a literal self-hash is a preimage problem. artifacts[0].bytes IS exact (zeroing does not change length). Recompute: read file, s/<64hex>/000...0/ at that field, sha256.
extensions.vendor_deviation: The catalog assigns ADV-0016 to openai/gpt-5-codex. It was executed by an Anthropic opus agent instead. Disclosed because the unit's reviewer_requirement asks for a cross-vendor ANTHROPIC opus refuter, which was written on the assumption of an OpenAI author -- against an Anthropic author the cross-vendor refuter should be OpenAI/Codex, or a genuinely fresh-context Anthropic agent that never saw this report.
